author: Jane Imbody
title: Nearly $100K raised at Dance Gala to preserve historic Marion home - NewsBreak
text:
By Jane Imbody Marion Star ,
11 hours ago The Marion Women’s Club and Hom e raised more than $98,000 at its 7th annual Celebrity Dance Gala, surpassing last year’s record.
Local businessman Cass Sisler was named “Overall Dance Champion” at the event, according to a community announcement. He danced with instructor Sarah Stalter to a medley of songs that featured a guitar solo and a cartwheel.
Jon Fetter and instructor Autumn Deeter, and Amanda Styer with instructor Kenny Creviston, received the “Judges Performance Awards” for their jive and Latin/salsa dances, respectively, according to the announcement.
Other local celebrity dancers participating in the charity fundraiser were Lily Lloyd, Sarah Hogan, Liz Feliciano, Robb Koons and Jay McDonald.
This year's theme was "Dancing in the Rain," with decorations designed by Terrie and Steve Phillips of Marion that featured umbrellas hanging from the ceiling as if they were floating in the air.
The annual fundraiser supports the preservation and maintenance of the Marion Women’s Club Historic Home and property.
“This overwhelming outpouring of support shows just how much our community believes in preserving and protecting the Marion Women’s Club Historic Home and property,” Club President and Gala Chair Valerie Wigton said, according to the announcement. “Many guests told me what an asset this piece of history is to our community.”
Proceeds to fund two improvement projects Money raised will be used to build a new back porch onto the north side of the historic home, replacing an unsafe and dilapidated porch.
Several falls have occurred on the current porch, making it a high priority in preservation efforts, according to Wigton.
In addition, the money will be used to pave the path leading from the neighboring AgCredit parking lot to the club’s historic home and auditorium.
Gala guests and renters use the lot for overflow parking, and paving the path will allow them to walk safely on a paved sidewalk, according to the announcement. Plans call for lighting and signage to be added along the path.
“We are so grateful to feature 44 sponsors and numerous in-kind donors this year – many who have been a part of this annual fundraiser since our first gala in 2019,” Wigton said. “Each year, we reach out to additional businesses and individuals in the community who are excited to be a part of the gala and eager to support the dancers involved. This year was no exception.”
About the Marion Women's Club & Home The historic home, built by Ida and Shauck Barlow in 1903, now features the Women’s History Resource Center, which was the original carriage house for the Barlows. Dedicated in 2025, the resource center houses the club’s complete collection of archives that date back to its founding in 1895. The archives are believed to be the most complete set of records featuring the women’s history movement in the United States.
The Marion Women’s Club is responsible for preserving and protecting the property, located at 1196 E. Center St. It is on the National Register of Historic Places and part of the “ReMARKable Ohio” bronze marker program.
Membership is open with $75 annual dues. For more information, visit MarionWomensClub.org .
